results.pair_summary: Both documents define the Intermediate Representation (IR) structure used in the runtime callback system. Document A provides the executable Common Lisp implementation with detailed comments describing guarantees and constraints. Document B provides a formal specification of the same interface, types, operations, and invariants (purity, immutability, ordering). They are semantically aligned but differ in artifact type (code vs. formal spec).
results.integration_rationale: Document A serves as the authoritative implementation within the Delta3 Kernel runtime, while Document B acts as a formal contract for verification. Maintaining both ensures that the executable logic (A) can be rigorously validated against the specified invariants (B), such as INV-PURITY and INV-IMMUTABLE, which are critical for deterministic replay and kernel integrity. Merging would either lose the machine-readable spec format or clutter the implementation with formal notation.
